title: Introduction to Automata Theory
overview: Study the core vocabulary: automaton and automata, automata theory, abstract machines, states, inputs, outputs, and the four major machine families.
objectives: Define automaton, automata theory, and abstract machine.
Use automaton and automata correctly as singular and plural.
Name the four major families and identify the simplest and most general models introduced.

keyTerms.definition: A formal model of a machine or computational process; automata is its plural.
A branch of computer science and mathematics that studies abstract models of computation and their behavior.
A simplified formal model that captures relevant computational behavior without requiring every physical implementation detail.
A condition or configuration of a machine that summarizes information relevant to its behavior.
A symbol or sequence of symbols supplied to a machine, typically drawn from a specified input alphabet.
A symbol or sequence of symbols a machine produces, when that model defines output behavior.
A system modeled through distinct events or values, often with signals sampled at separate time points.
A highly general formal model of computation, introduced in this lesson as one of four machine families.
The term used in the source for a machine model implemented in software.
Finite-state machine, pushdown automata, linear-bounded automata, and Turing machine.

segments.title: Why study automata?
notes: Automata theory lets us reason systematically about what a machine does without first building or inspecting its hardware.
A model helps explain how a system solves a problem and how an input can affect its behavior.
The lecture connects this way of thinking to designing repeatable systems, including computers and aircraft autopilot systems.
segments.speakerNotes: Pag-aralan ang behavior ng machine kahit wala sa harap natin ang mismong hardware. Nakakatulong ang model sa pag-intindi kung paano nagiging output ang inputs at kung paano gumagawa ng repeatable actions ang isang system.
segments.visualDescription: Slides titled “WHY WE STUDY AUTOMATA” show bullets about reasoning without hardware detail and understanding how machines solve problems, alongside pictures of computer, phone, industrial automation, and laboratory equipment.

segments.title: A thermostat as a small state-based example
notes: The thermostat example has two named states: on and off.
It checks surrounding temperature and changes operation in response to a temperature condition.
The example demonstrates how a simple model can describe behavior while larger computing systems may involve many more states and inputs.
segments.speakerNotes: Sa thermostat example, on at off ang dalawang states. Nagbabago ang operation depende sa temperature condition. Mas komplikado ang computer dahil mas marami ang inputs at posibleng states.
segments.visualDescription: A thermostat slide shows an on/off control and the two-state idea; surrounding examples include a pendulum clock, missile guidance, and telephone networks.

segments.title: Automaton, automata, and automatic devices
notes: The word automata is presented as referring to self-acting or automatic machines; automaton is singular and automata plural.
An elevator illustrates input and response: selecting a floor prompts the system to act toward that floor.
The speaker also uses choosing a television channel, typing a character, and entering an ATM PIN to illustrate input-driven behavior.
A formal automaton is a model of behavior; a physical elevator, TV, or ATM is a real system that may be modeled in many ways.
segments.speakerNotes: Automaton ang singular at automata ang plural. Ipinapakita ng elevator, TV at ATM examples kung paano may automatic na response sa isang input.
segments.visualDescription: The slide gives the Greek-root/“self-acting” explanation and singular/plural labels. A photo of an elevator and a small state diagram appear, followed by images of automated devices.

segments.title: Automata theory and abstract machine models
notes: Automata theory is introduced as a theoretical area of computer science and mathematics concerned with mathematical models of computation.
Abstract models let us analyze how a system behaves without tying the reasoning to one physical implementation.
The lecture describes a model in terms of inputs, outputs, and operations; it uses a banking-system model with deposit, withdrawal, and transfer operations.
The Turing machine is introduced as a particularly general and powerful abstract model.
The speaker distinguishes a model implemented in software (called a virtual machine in the slide) from a hardware implementation.
segments.speakerNotes: Ang automata theory ay tungkol sa abstract machine models. Sa model, puwedeng pag-aralan ang inputs, outputs at operations nang hindi kailangang isama ang lahat ng hardware details.
segments.visualDescription: Slides define theory as study of abstract machines; a banking example lists deposit/withdraw/transfer. Later slides show large state-machine illustrations, a Turing-machine label, and “virtual machine” versus “machine” implementation labels.
segments.caution: An abstract machine is a mathematical model, not necessarily a runnable software virtual machine. Also, hardware implementation does not by itself make an abstract model “a machine”; implementation and formal model are different levels.

segments.title: The objective: describe and analyze discrete behavior
notes: The stated objective is to develop methods for describing and analyzing the dynamic behavior of discrete systems.
The slide mentions signals sampled periodically as one way such systems may be represented.
segments.speakerNotes: Layunin na magkaroon ng paraan para ilarawan at suriin ang pagbabago ng behavior ng discrete systems. Ang note na ito ay buod, hindi eksaktong salita ng speaker.
segments.visualDescription: A slide titled “OBJECTIVE OF AUTOMATA THEORY” summarizes methods for describing and analyzing dynamic behavior of discrete systems with periodically sampled signals.

segments.title: Inputs, outputs, and states
notes: Inputs and outputs are described as sequences of symbols chosen from finite sets (alphabets).
The state set depends on the particular machine model.
A block diagram shows an input sequence entering an automaton and an output sequence leaving it, with states inside the machine.
Treat these as common modeling dimensions, not a universal promise that every automaton produces an output sequence.
segments.speakerNotes: Tatlong characteristics ang ipinapakita: inputs, outputs at states. Ang kahulugan ng state ay nakadepende sa klase ng machine model na pinag-aaralan.
segments.visualDescription: A “CHARACTERISTICS OF MACHINES” slide lists inputs, outputs, and states; a subsequent block diagram routes an input sequence through an automaton with internal states to an output sequence.
segments.caution: The diagram is a broad machine-model picture. Many standard finite automata are acceptors: they classify an input string as accepted or rejected instead of emitting an arbitrary output string. Output behavior depends on the chosen model.

segments.title: Four major families of automata
notes: The lesson names finite-state machines, pushdown automata, linear-bounded automata, and Turing machines.
The closing narration presents them in an increasing-complexity hierarchy, from finite-state machines toward Turing machines.
This is a first-pass orientation; later lessons are needed to compare their memory, computational power, and formal definitions.
segments.speakerNotes: Apat na families ang binanggit: finite-state machine, pushdown automata, linear-bounded automata at Turing machine. Ipinapakita sila bilang mas simple hanggang mas general na computational models.
segments.visualDescription: A slide lists the four families in order and briefly highlights finite-state machine at the beginning and Turing machine at the end.
segments.caution: “Complexity” here is an informal teaching shorthand. The formal distinctions are about computational resources and language-recognition power, not simply how complicated a physical machine looks.

recap: Automaton is singular; automata is plural.
Automata theory studies abstract machine models and their behavior.
Inputs, outputs (where defined), and states describe machine behavior.
The four families are finite-state machines, pushdown automata, linear-bounded automata, and Turing machines.
The introductory ordering starts with finite-state machines and ends with Turing machines.
commonMistakes: Treating the physical device as identical to its abstract model.
Assuming every automaton emits an output sequence; some models only accept or reject strings.
Using automata as a singular noun instead of automaton.
Interpreting the four-family ordering as a complete formal account of their power.

questions.prompt: Which term refers to a symbol or sequence of symbols supplied to a machine?

questions.prompt: What does a finite set of states mean?
choices: There is a fixed finite collection of possible states
A new state must be created for every input symbol read
The machine cannot read an input string longer than its number of states
Every state must produce a different output symbol
questions.explanation: The state set is finite; a run can revisit states while processing input. This does not require one new state per symbol.
